title: Studio route ownership and local connector
summary: Route-counted ownership for the Angular Studio, its local connector and the remote Task Server (B1, decided 7 September 2026). The AGT-3017 extension classifies 36 Git, checkout and repository routes plus 41 repository-document routes. It proposes immutable SHA-keyed diff objects computed on the runner host and served by the Task Server, retires the blocked manual commit routes, and moves branch maintenance to a runner-host request. Following the operator steer of 5 October, it makes hand interventions an explicit, leased and attributed attempt in a central container on the runner host, with VS Code attached over Remote-SSH. Under that option the Windows dev seat keeps no Git route. Decisions D1 to D8 are pending, each with a recommended working option.
statusReason: Reopened by AGT-3017 on 2026-10-05 for the Git views and diffs extension and the intervention workspace steer (sections 07 to 18). The B1 decision of 2026-09-07 and its delivered P0 to P3 route migration stay recorded; AGT-W49 still owns the Operations Server destination.

implementationTasks.title: Interim guard for dev-seat Git views
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 1 of the AGT-3017 extension in `docs/studio-route-ownership/index.html` (section 12, decision D6).

In OrchestratorApi, `GET /api/tasks/{taskId}/git/status`, `/git/diff` and `/git/file` (`backend/Features/Tasks/TaskGitEndpoints.cs:25-45`) fall back to the main checkout through `GitService.ResolveRunLocation` when no local task worktree exists. Change them so that a task without a local `task/<id>` worktree answers a typed `unavailable` result with reason `no-local-worktree` instead of reading the main checkout. Add the resolved repository root kind (`task-worktree` or `main-checkout`) and HEAD SHA to every task commit, diff, status and hygiene response, and show that provenance in the Angular Git pane. Open a `GitProcessTelemetry.BeginRequest` scope for every route in section 08 so their spawns appear in `/api/admin/git-telemetry`.

Acceptance: regression tests prove a task without a local worktree never returns main-checkout status or diff. A Playwright check shows the provenance label in light and dark themes. Telemetry lists the new route labels. No route classification changes.

implementationTasks.title: Git object contract and Task Server store
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 2 of the AGT-3017 extension in `docs/studio-route-ownership/index.html` (sections 09 and 15, decisions D1 and D5, working option A for both).

Add versioned contracts in `contracts/TaskServer.Contracts` for immutable Git objects keyed by `repositoryId`, `baseSha`, `headSha`, diff options and renderer version. Supported kinds: `commit`, `reviewed-delivery`, `integration`, `run-checkpoint`. Each object has a manifest (path, status, rename source, numstat, binary flag, truncation flag) and one patch per file. Add a Task Server `git_objects` index table and store manifest and patch bodies in the existing artifact store with content hashing. Add read routes that never start Git: object by key, manifest page by cursor, and one file patch. They answer `ready`, `warming`, `unavailable` with a typed reason, or `too-large`. Retention follows the owning task and result ref, not memory pressure. Start limits at 5,000 manifest files and 256 KiB or 5,000 lines per file patch, configurable, and record the measured size distribution of the last 200 deliveries in the card result.

Acceptance: contract tests for keys, states, paging and limits. Ingestion is idempotent per key. Reads spawn no process. Existing artifact limits are enforced.

implementationTasks.title: Runner publication of Git facts and diff objects
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 3 of the AGT-3017 extension in `docs/studio-route-ownership/index.html` (sections 09 and 15, decisions D1 and D5).

Extend the runner so that the host that owns the canonical checkout and run worktrees publishes Git objects through the card 2 contract. Publish at run completion (one `commit` object per commit in the delivery range, first-parent for merges), at review material creation (`reviewed-delivery` with the merge-base, Result-SHA and review truncation state from `runner/RemoteReviewWorkspace.cs`), after each agent turn, before handoff, and on salvage (`run-checkpoint` of the worktree against the run base, including untracked files within limits). Add one fenced runner operation, `git.object`, that computes a missing object on request. Deduplicate requests per key and cap Git child processes per repository. Extend `DurableGitFactsPayload` or add a sibling outbox item; do not move Git into the Task Server.

Acceptance: integration tests with a real repository prove that objects match `git diff` output byte for byte within limits, that truncation is explicit, that duplicate requests produce one computation, and that the review object records the same merge-base and Result-SHA the review prompt used.

implementationTasks.title: Central task commit, diff and run views
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 4 of the AGT-3017 extension in `docs/studio-route-ownership/index.html` (section 08 task rows, decisions D1 and D2).

Serve these through Task Server v1 from card 2 objects: the task commit, aggregate and per-SHA files, diff and file reads (fe-277 to fe-283), provenance (fe-314), task Git hygiene (fe-300), and the run commits, diff and files routes (fe-325, fe-327, fe-328). Serve the run-checkpoint view for status, diff and file (fe-301, fe-297, fe-298). Read the attributed `commits[]` from the Task Server task record, and add it to the completion projection if it is missing. Move the lazy attribution backfill out of GET handlers. In Angular, label every diff with its object kind and both SHAs, page by manifest cursor, and load one file patch at a time. Keep `reviewed-delivery` and attributed commits as separate, named views.

Acceptance: the Studio task Git and commit views work through the connector with the Windows checkout absent. A Playwright proof covers light and dark themes, a truncated large diff and a `warming` state. No Angular task diff call reaches a dev-seat route.

implementationTasks.title: Central project Git views
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 5 of the AGT-3017 extension in `docs/studio-route-ownership/index.html` (section 08 project rows, decisions D1 and D5).

Publish versioned project Git facts from the runner host's canonical checkout on every fetch that moves a ref: the ref inventory, history pages, integration state, and a commit and path index. Serve them from Task Server v1 to replace `/api/git/inventory`, `/history`, `/integration`, `/project-commit/files` and `/diff` (fe-090, fe-092 to fe-095), checkout history and file-at-SHA (fe-271, and fe-270 with `at`), wiki history and revisions (fe-194, fe-201), and `/api/search/repository` (fe-246). Use card 2 objects for commit diffs. Facts are immutable rows keyed by repository and ref signature. Reads never start Git, and a stale snapshot is labelled with its generation time.

Acceptance: each replaced view works through the connector with the Windows checkout absent. Paging is bounded where today's `git log --follow` has no limit. Tests prove no read spawns a process.

implementationTasks.title: Repository maintenance as a runner-host request
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 6 of the AGT-3017 extension in `docs/studio-route-ownership/index.html` (section 10, decision D3, working option A).

Replace the Studio's Git cleanup and branch-sweep routes (fe-082 to fe-089) with one Task Server operator request, `repository-maintenance`, that has a plan phase and an execute phase. A fenced runner operation runs it on the runner host's canonical checkout under the AGT-W18 per-project ref-mutation lease. The plan is an operation artifact that the Task Server serves, so no GET fetches. Execution re-checks every ref tip and ancestry, deletes only planned refs with expected-old protection, and writes a receipt. Move branch-sweep settings to Task Server project settings, and serve reports from operation history. Requests carry operator identity, a request key and an expected generation.

Acceptance: plan and execute work with the Studio detached. A moved ref tip aborts that ref's deletion. Every deletion has a receipt. The 24 h retention sweep and the operator request share one implementation.

implementationTasks.title: Retire dev-seat Git routes and reclassify the inventory
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 7 of the AGT-3017 extension in `docs/studio-route-ownership/index.html` (sections 08, 10 and 13, decisions D2, D3, D4 and D7, working option A for D2 to D4 and option b for D7). Start after cards 4 to 6 and the intervention cards 9 to 12 have landed.

Remove the Angular calls and OrchestratorApi Studio handlers for `POST /api/tasks/{taskId}/git/commit`, `/git/commit-accepted-evidence` and `/git/generate-message`, and for the routes the dossier marks Retire. Remove the dev-seat Git routes that cards 4 to 6 replaced from the connector allowlist. Update `docs/studio-route-ownership/build-inventory.mjs` classification rules so that regenerating `routes.json` yields the section 08 owners. Never hand-edit `routes.json`. Keep `routes-inventory.test.mjs` green and update the connector route checksum. Replace `POST /api/tasks/{taskId}/open-in-vscode` with the `vscode://vscode-remote/ssh-remote+intervene-<slot>/<path>` link that card 13 renders from the Task Server intervention record. If the operator selected D7 option a or d (and therefore D4 option B) instead, keep only the labelled local status, diff, file and open-in-vscode routes, without task fallback.

Acceptance: the regenerated `routes.json` has no dev-seat route that runs Git, other than any D4 option B routes. The connector startup check passes. No Angular call reaches a removed route.

implementationTasks.title: Concept: repository document writes under the remote publisher
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Concept card for the follow-up named in section 11 of `docs/studio-route-ownership/index.html` (decision D4). Run in concept mode and deliver a Dossier.

Wiki writes commit directly to the Windows checkout's current branch (`ProjectDocsService.CommitWikiChange`). Dossier review, decision and document writes commit and queue a push through `ManagedRepositoryMutationService`. Catalogue reads can assign Dossier keys and commit (`WorkbenchCatalogueService.EnsureCanonicalKeys`). Security writes leave the checkout dirty. Design the repository-write contract that `docs/operations/remote-task-server-local-studio.md` plans for these producers under the AGT-W18 single-publisher rule. Cover reads from a published document snapshot, writes as operator requests that become platform commits, conflict handling against a moving integration branch, key assignment outside reads, and the interim while the Windows checkout still serves documents.

Acceptance: a decision-pending Dossier with alternatives, recommendation, evidence and open decisions, and implementation cards sized as bounded slices.

implementationTasks.title: Intervention attempt kind and exclusive lease
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 9 of the AGT-3017 extension in `docs/studio-route-ownership/index.html` (section 13 "Exclusive lease", decisions D7 option b and D6 option A).

Add the attempt kind `intervention` beside `coding` and `review` in `contracts/TaskServer.Contracts/RunnerContracts.cs` and the Task Server store. Add operator requests `intervention.open` (card key, start point `card-head` or a named salvage ref, operator identity, request key) and `intervention.release` (mode `send-to-review`, `hand-back` with a required prompt, or `discard`). A claim uses the existing per-task `fence_counters` sequence, so the intervention holds the newest fence; the hosting runner operation renews the lease, and Studio detach never drops it.

Conflict rules: on a live coding attempt, `open` with `stopFirst=true` records the stop through the existing remote stop store, waits for the release, then claims; without it the request is refused with the holder named. On a live review or integration attempt the request queues visibly until the verdict or release. Pickup and follow-ups queue behind the intervention as today. Stale writes from the stopped attempt keep failing with `StaleFence`.

Release: `send-to-review` completes with the intervention Result-SHA and moves the card to `4-auto-review`; `hand-back` writes a continuation base with source `intervention` so the next coding round starts from the intervention Result-SHA, not the integration head; `discard` keeps only the salvage ref and returns the card to its previous lane. An idle or maximum-lifetime expiry releases as discard, parks the card and raises an escalation item; it never continues automatically. While here, make a stopped run's queued follow-up use its salvage as continuation base or remove the misleading comment at `runner/RemoteTaskRunner.cs:861-864`, and record which.

Acceptance: integration tests for claim order, stop-and-take, queueing behind review, `StaleFence` for the stopped attempt's late completion and ref, each release mode, the hand-back base, and expiry parking. The intervention never takes the AGT-W18 ref-mutation lease.

implementationTasks.title: Intervention workspace provisioning on the runner host
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 10 of the AGT-3017 extension in `docs/studio-route-ownership/index.html` (section 13 "Provisioning", decision D7 option b).

Add fenced runner operations `intervention.open` and `intervention.close` through the existing `studio_operations` contract. Open: prepare the worktree through the same `GitWorkspace.PrepareAsync` path as coding runs, at the card branch HEAD (`origin/runner/<runnerId>/<taskKey>`, else the latest Result-SHA) or the requested salvage ref, at `$RUNNER_WORKDIR/<project>/worktrees/<taskKey>`, with lease kind `intervention`. Run `.agent-studio/prepare` through `ProjectPreparationExecutor` with the shared cache, exactly as for agents (AGT-W51: the script is the truth, the image only accelerates). Start a container through the C1 launcher in `docs/operations/container-tranche-plan.md` (`--rm --init --user`, `--pull=never`, label `agent-studio.attempt`, worktree and clone bind-mounted at identical paths). Use an `intervention` target in `runner/Dockerfile` with the toolchain, Git and `sshd`, and no runner daemon, push credentials or provider credentials. Apply CPU and memory limits under the delegated cgroup slice so the co-hosted Task Server keeps its share. No Docker socket is exposed to anything but the runner daemon.

Lifecycle: admission requires at least 25 GiB free and fewer than two active interventions per host (one per operator), all configurable. Idle means no SSH session and no worktree change: warn at 1 h, close at 4 h, hard maximum 24 h with one extension. Close commits a dirty tree under the operator identity as `wip(intervention): ...` to a fenced salvage ref, removes the container, and removes the worktree only after the Task Server acknowledges the ref. No tarballs. Report active interventions, idle time and disk use per intervention in remote-host telemetry, with a 10 GiB soft budget warning.

Acceptance: integration tests on a real repository for open at card HEAD and at a salvage ref, prepare parity with a coding run, refusal on low disk and full slots, idle close with salvage, and cleanup after acknowledgement. Document the operations in `docs/operations/setup/linux-runner-host.md`.

implementationTasks.title: Remote-SSH attach for intervention workspaces
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 11 of the AGT-3017 extension in `docs/studio-route-ownership/index.html` (section 13 "Attach path", decision D8 option A).

On the runner host, add a host account `intervene` with no shell whose `authorized_keys` entries are `restrict,port-forwarding,permitopen="127.0.0.1:<slot port>"` for the configured slots, so it can only serve as a `ProxyJump`. Register each operator's public key in the Task Server user profile and write it into the container's `sshd` at open; remove it at close. `sshd` in the intervention container listens on `127.0.0.1:<slot port>` with a pinned host key that the Task Server records. Use two slots with static aliases `intervene-1` and `intervene-2`. Generate the per-operator SSH config block (ProxyJump to the host alias, pinned known-hosts entries) and the `vscode://vscode-remote/ssh-remote+intervene-<slot>/<worktree path>` link from the intervention record. Audit SSH session start and end as intervention timeline events.

Acceptance: tests or a scripted host check prove that the `intervene` account cannot get a shell, cannot open ports outside the slots, and cannot reach the Docker socket; that a closed intervention refuses connections; and that VS Code Remote-SSH opens the worktree with the C# and TypeScript extensions running in the container. Document onboarding in `docs/operations/setup/`, including the admin-SSH emergency path.

implementationTasks.title: Intervention commit attribution and checkpoints
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 12 of the AGT-3017 extension in `docs/studio-route-ownership/index.html` (section 13 "Attribution" and "Diffs", decisions D7 option b and D1 option A).

Set the container's Git author and committer from the operator's Task Server user record. Install a `commit-msg` hook through the container's global `core.hooksPath` (agent worktrees unaffected) that appends `Task-Id: <key>`, `Attempt-Id: <intervention attempt>` and `Intervention: <operator user id>`. At release, treat every commit in base..Result-SHA as belonging to the intervention, even without the trailer. Add `author` and `provenance` (`agent`, `intervention`, `platform`) to `TaskCommitInfo` and its Task Server projection, and set `RunAttemptId` to the intervention attempt. In `RemoteCommitAttributionGuard`, relax the other-task-key subject rejection for intervention commits, and flag commits in agent ranges whose author is neither the runner identity nor an intervention attempt. Add per-commit provenance to the review prompt material without changing the reviewed range. Publish `run-checkpoint` objects for the intervention at each commit, at most every 5 minutes while the tree changes, and at release, through card 3's contract; until card 3 lands, skip checkpoints and keep attribution.

Acceptance: tests prove that human commits appear in `commits[]` with author and provenance `intervention`, in the review range and in the gate input; that a commit without the trailer is still attributed; that a subject mentioning another task key no longer rejects an intervention range; and that the card timeline shows each intervention commit.

implementationTasks.title: Studio Intervene action and ad-hoc intervention cards
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 13 of the AGT-3017 extension in `docs/studio-route-ownership/index.html` (section 13 "Work without a card", decisions D7 option b and D8 option A). Start after cards 9 to 11.

Add an "Intervene" action to the task detail. It shows the current holder, offers "Stop and intervene" when a coding attempt runs, shows the queued state behind a review, and sends `intervention.open`. While an intervention is active, show its state, slot, idle time, the latest intervention checkpoint (labelled "Intervention" with its time), the `vscode://` link, and a one-time SSH config block to copy. Add a release dialog with the three modes; hand back requires a prompt. Add "Intervene without a card": it creates a card with a required title, no prompt and the tag `intervention`, then opens the workspace on a new branch from the integration head. Add a board filter for the `intervention` tag. Use central design tokens and existing components; no left accent bars.

Acceptance: Playwright proof in light and dark themes for the idle, active, queued and release states, and for ad-hoc creation. The Studio never calls a dev-seat route for this flow, and no Studio route starts a local process.
